corrections.why: The 1884 date belongs to the earlier pierhead and the octagonal iron tower placed on it in 1885; the present conical tower was lit in 1911.
1831 is the beacon on the river's east pier, 1875 the pier towers; the present West Pierhead station dates from 1911 (USLHS 'Year Established: 1911').

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1884 and 1875 events are earlier lights on the west breakwater/west pier; GSA says built 1910, other sources say lit March 1911.

notes_for_editor: No NRHP text (placeholder only), no Lighthouse Board 1909-1910 reports in corpus, and no newspaper hits; 1911 construction rests on LighthouseFriends plus USLHS. Conflicts: construction year 1910 (GSA) vs lit 25 Mar 1911; lens (LHF: removed c.1995, on display at Great Lakes Science Center; 2023 news quoting NRHP: still in tower); material (cast iron per LHF; USLHS cast iron/brick/wood; GSA brick sheathed in wood). The Wahnapitae keeper Hatch was at the earlier breakwater light, not the 1911 tower; Hatch dates 1885-1914 come from LHF, 1911-1914 at the new station from USLHS. Page numbers for LSS 1891 (pp. 21-24) read from the OCR page markers; check on the scan. Commissioner 1918 p.74 and 1915 p.57 from corpus grep printed pages. Bulletin index entry cited to the index, not the issue; Bulletin p.250 not read. Owners of the 2023 sale deliberately not named. Roster lines for third and fourth assistants, laborer and Coast Guard crew added from the USLHS page at fact-check. The 'Frank S. Huntington' fourth assistant 1916 and third assistant 1916-1917 are the same name on the USLHS page; the Milius entry is a single name. LHF gives the fog signal building as 29 by 30 feet, the Commissioner's report 29 by 31.
